trust_decision.summary: Which keys taken from rule condition field names may be written as own properties into the plain object built by rulesToFields. setByPath decides this with a denylist (__proto__/constructor/prototype) and walks intermediates with `res[prop] || {}`, which follows inherited builtins (toString, hasOwnProperty, valueOf) and caller-owned non-plain values (functions, arrays).

landing_point.why: The summary names rulesToFields and setByPath. setByPath is the only path-walking setter in the package, and its existing FORBIDDEN_PROPERTIES denylist (utils.ts:10) points straight at it.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API rulesToFields(ability, action, subjectType) from @casl/ability/extra (setByPath itself is not exported: packages/casl-ability/src/index.ts:37-42)

fix_sites.module_kind: public extra helper (root accumulator changed from {} to Object.create(null))

fix_sites.entry_point: public API rulesToFields (return type AnyObject -> NullObject, type-only)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Both runtime changes sit in the same call chain the summary names (rulesToFields.ts:28 -> utils.ts:21). setByPath has no other caller (only use: packages/casl-ability/src/extra/rulesToFields.ts:23).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could argue the root accumulator (rulesToFields.ts:28) needs no change: a final key like `toString` on a plain {} root only creates an own property, and FORBIDDEN_PROPERTIES already blocks __proto__. So they would fix only the setByPath walk.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate dotted paths must keep merging into shared intermediates (`state.private` + `state.owner.id`). Own object intermediates that are not plain (Date, class instance, null-proto object) must be kept and extended, not replaced. Plain-object values (mongo operators such as $in) must still be skipped. Over-broad fixes break these: replacing every intermediate, rejecting any key that exists on Object.prototype, or throwing.

O6_input_shapes: inherited builtin as intermediate at root: `toString.call`, `hasOwnProperty.call`, `valueOf.call` (fix.diff:60-94)
inherited builtin as intermediate in a nested path: `state.toString.call` (fix.diff:64-65)
own function value as intermediate: { field: fn, 'field.call': ... } (fix.diff:96-107)
primitive or nullish intermediate: 0, false, '', 'value', 1, null, undefined (fix.diff:147-159)
array intermediate, must not be mutated (fix.diff:161-172)
builtin names as final key at root and nested: must become own properties, with the prototype unchanged (fix.diff:109-127)
denylisted final keys __proto__/constructor/prototype at root and nested, with a null-proto result (fix.diff:129-145)

O7_producer.where: Condition keys come straight from caller rules (createMongoAbility / ability.update, or unpackRules at packages/casl-ability/src/extra/packRules.ts:41-61, which passes conditions through unchanged). No producer shapes the polluting state; the cause is in setByPath itself.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An unpackRules variant that expands dotted condition keys or merges packed conditions into a fresh {} with a hand-rolled path setter (not setByPath)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Packed rules are the documented way to ship rules from server to client as JSON. Normalising conditions on unpack is a plausible maintainer feature, and a second, separate path setter would be a distant second implementation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A mongoose helper that builds a default document from rulesToFields-like condition values with its own nested set over schema paths
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The mongoose integration already reads schema paths. A 'defaults for new document' helper in that package would reimplement the dotted set in another package.

O9_family: prototype pollution (CWE-1321) via set-by-path on caller-controlled dotted keys; builtin-function mutation through an inherited-property walk
